extracted.intended_audience: children's book writers and illustrators, SCBWI members, publishing professionals, and readers interested in children's/YA literature awards
extracted.subtask_description: An announcement of the 2025 SCBWI Golden Kite Awards and the Sid Fleischman Award for Humor listing winners and honor recipients across award categories for children's and young adult books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award values / criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Golden Kite Awards celebrates the best in children's storytelling, honoring excellence, creativity, and inspiration across genres and age groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This phrasing indicates the qualities the awards seek to recognize (excellence, creativity, inspiration) but the page does not provide further formal judging criteria or scoring rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sid Fleischman Award for Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Sid Fleischman Award for Humor — WINNER: Harriet Tells the Truth by Elana K. Arnold (Walden Pond Press); HONOR: On a Wing and a Tear by Cynthia Leitich Smith (Heartdrum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named award recognizing humor in children's/YA literature (implicit criterion: excellence in humor). The page lists the winner and honor book but does not provide detailed judging standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Book Text
rubrics_metrics.description: Picture Book Text — WINNER: The Man Who Didn't Like Animals written by Deborah Underwood, illustrated by LeUyen Pham (Clarion Books); HONOR: The Night Market written by Seina Wedlick, illustrated by Briana Mukodiri Uchendu (Random House Studio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes text (writing) for picture books. Winners and honor recipients are listed as examples; no further scoring rubric is provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Book Illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: Picture Book Illustration — WINNER: The One and Only Googoosh, illustrated and written by Azadeh Westergaard (Viking Books for Young Readers); HONOR: Eloisa's Magical Window, illustrated by John Parra, written by Margarita Engle (Atheneum Books for Young Readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes illustration for picture books (visual/artistic quality). The page lists winners/honors but gives no detailed evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction Text for Younger Readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonfiction Text for Younger Readers — WINNER: Ida B. Wells Marches for the Vote written by Dinah Johnson, illustrated by Jeremy Jordan (Christy Ottaviano Books-Little Brown and Hachette); HONOR: Comet Chaser: The True Cinderella Story of Caroline Herschel ... written by Pamela S. Turner, illustrated by Vivien Mildenberger (Chronicle Books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes nonfiction writing targeted at younger readers; examples provided but no explicit rubric on accuracy, sourcing, or age-appropriateness beyond the category label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction Text for Older Readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonfiction Text for Older Readers — WINNER: Rising From the Ashes: Los Angeles 1992. Edward Jae Song Lee, Latasha Harlins, Rodney King, and a City On Fire by Paula Yoo (Norton Young Readers); HONOR: Uprooted: A Memoir About What Happens When Your Family Moves Back by Ruth Chan (Roaring Brook Press).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes nonfiction for older readers/YA; page gives winners/honors as exemplars but no scoring guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle Grade Fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Middle Grade Fiction — WINNER: The Other Side of Tomorrow written by Tina Cho, art by Deb JJ Lee (Harper/Alley); HONOR: The Bletchley Riddle by Ruta Sepetys and Steve Sheinkin (Viking Books for Young Readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes fiction for middle-grade readers; page lists winners/honors without providing explicit evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrated Book for Older Readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated Book for Older Readers — WINNER: Uprooted: A Memoir About What Happens When Your Family Moves Back by Ruth Chan (Roaring Brook Press); HONOR: Meet Me on Mercer Street by Bookie Vivat (Scholastic Press).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes books that combine illustration and text aimed at older readers; winners/honors shown but no formal rubric provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Young Adult Fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Young Adult Fiction — WINNER: Girls Like Her by Melanie Sumrow (Balzer + Bray); HONOR: Kill Her Twice by Stacey Lee (G.P. Putnam's Sons Books for Young Readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes fiction targeted at young adult readers; page provides winners/honors but does not detail judging criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary awards / prize amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The winner in each category received $2,500. Each honor recipient received $500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies the financial awards associated with winning or receiving an honor in the listed categories; it is administrative information rather than judging criteria but is presented alongside the award results.
